verdict: Monopolies Vol. II is a masterclass in using game mechanics as conspiracy education — every POWER line is a real financial crime turned into a playable move. The deck's 14-phase architecture gives it an overwhelming structural coherence that makes it feel like a complete exposé in card form. Named strength: Phase 7 Holy Money & Wet Work (Roberto Calvi, Sindona's Espresso) is some of the best Kayfabizarro content in the entire corpus. Named weakness: Page 12 Digital Panopticon phase suffers from design-heavy layouts that obscure text — Crypto-Colonialism and Cashless Trap need text clarity. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 cards mapping every financial crime from the Riksbank to CBDCs. For anyone who's ever wondered how the game is actually rigged — and wanted to play as the house.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: MONOPOLIES, MANIPULATION & MURDER VOL. II – Every Financial Crime Is a Playable Move (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Two of the bankers in this deck were murdered before they could talk. The rest are still collecting interest.

It opens in 1668 with the first central bank and it never stops: Napoleon weaponizing inflation against his enemies, J.P. Morgan triggering the panic he then heroically solved, Nixon unpegging the dollar from gold on a Sunday night in 1971, the Vatican's own bank laundering money through a corpse left hanging under Blackfriars Bridge. Line the dates up and the isolated scandals resolve into one continuous institution, 350 years on the same payroll. The opponent here is the reflex that reads each crime as its own freak accident, when the through-line is the actual product.

56 cut-and-play cards hand you every move in that machine and dare you to run it yourself: establish the monopoly, manufacture the panic, wash the drug money into clean Treasury bonds, freeze the protester's account before breakfast. You do not study the crime. You perform it, out loud, until the whole table can see exactly how the trick holds.
